data.title: CSI Unveils Commercial Suite to Enable Community Banks to Attract and Grow Business Relationships
data.description:
New suite gives community banks the business digital banking, real-time ledgering, multi-rail payments, and card capabilities they need to win and retain complex commercial relationships

PADUCAH, Ky.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- CSI, a leading provider of end-to-end financial software and technology, today announced CSI Commercial Suite, designed to help community banks compete for larger and more complex business customers. The suite combines modern deposit, payment, card, and treasury capabilities in prepackaged solutions, pre-integrated with CSI’s core and digital banking platforms and connecting directly to the accounting and ERP systems businesses use daily.

Businesses increasingly expect modern payment and cash management capabilities, and many will change banks to get them. According to Datos Insights, half of community bank customers are now open to switching financial institutions within two years, and those who move cite better functionality, not price, as the reason. For a community bank, that means deposits, fee revenue, and daily financial work are at risk of migrating to larger institutions over time.

In its latest research, Datos also found that the top cash flow complaint among community bank customers is managing multiple systems that don't communicate with each other. CSI is helping community banks address this fragmentation by delivering the modern capabilities that keep them at the center of how businesses manage and move money.

“Businesses outgrow basic cash management well before they outgrow their bank,” said Gilles Ubaghs, executive advisor with the Commercial Banking & Payments practice at Datos Insights. “The banks that close that gap with more connected capabilities are better placed to keep commercial relationships they'd otherwise be at risk of losing.”

CSI is initially packaging these capabilities around commercial markets where community banks already hold the relationship and local knowledge, but where operational requirements have historically pushed the business toward larger institutions. These include homeowners and community associations, landlords and property management companies, attorney and client trusts, and title companies. CSI is also delivering cash management and liquidity capabilities that span markets, providing businesses with multi-entity treasury operations, real-time balance visibility, and automated reconciliation.

While each industry has distinct requirements, they share underlying needs around fund segregation, payment controls, reconciliation, and reporting. CSI is bringing those capabilities together on a common technology foundation, enabling banks to support specialized commercial workflows without the burden of managing multiple vendors and complex commercial integrations.

“Community banks are the operating infrastructure of local economies, and every commercial relationship they can’t fully serve means deposits, treasury activity, and eventually lending capacity leaving the community for a bigger bank,” said Nancy Langer, president and CEO of CSI. “With this suite, we’re giving community banks the sophisticated capabilities their business customers now expect, so they can keep those relationships and the local economic activity that comes with them.”

CSI Commercial Suite brings together several capabilities supporting commercial financial operations, including:

  • Real-time ledgering and virtual account management, enabling businesses to organize and track funds by entity, property, client, transaction, or purpose while giving the bank a single, consolidated view of the relationship
  • Multi-rail payment orchestration, supporting payment activity across ACH, wire, the RTP® network, the FedNow® Service, and card rails
  • Commercial card capabilities, including debit, prepaid, virtual, and corporate card programs with configurable controls
  • Digital banking and treasury capabilities, including dashboards, payment approvals, user permissions, mobile banking, and APIs
  • Embedded banking through direct API integration with industry-specific ERP systems
  • Automated allocation, reconciliation, and reporting, helping reduce manual processes while providing greater visibility into balances and transaction activity
  • Operational controls, including audit trails, positive pay, activity monitoring, and configurable governance

The announcement follows CSI’s July 2026 acquisition of payments infrastructure provider Qolo and builds on CSI’s multi-year investment in commercial banking technology. Qolo’s technology serves as the orchestration layer of CSI Commercial Suite across payments, accounts, and workflows, integrating with CSI’s core, digital banking, and broader API capabilities.

Harmony Bank, a community bank serving businesses and consumers in Northeast Texas, will be among the first to take advantage of CSI Commercial Suite, with a focus on supporting banking for homeowners associations (HOAs) and other community associations.

“Commercial clients want relationship banking and technology that fits how they operate, especially in HOA and community association banking, where managing hundreds of associations creates complex account, payment, and reconciliation needs,” said Kara Fox, senior vice president, director of Signature Solutions at Harmony Bank. “The same is true for property managers, law firms, healthcare practices, and municipalities. CSI Commercial Suite will give banks like ours the ability to grow alongside the associations, businesses, and communities we serve.”

CSI plans to introduce CSI Commercial Suite capabilities in a phased rollout beginning in Q2 of 2027.

To learn more about CSI Commercial Suite, register for CSI’s upcoming introductory webinar, scheduled for Tuesday, September 22, 2026, or visit https://www.csiweb.com/commercial-suite/.

About CSI

CSI is a leading provider of end-to-end financial technology solutions, helping U.S. community and regional financial institutions compete and grow. Backed by more than 60 years of industry expertise, CSI delivers a comprehensive suite of capabilities spanning core banking, digital banking, lending, payments, risk and compliance, and managed IT and cybersecurity services. CSI gives financial institutions the flexibility to deploy an open, fully integrated core platform or best-of-breed, core-agnostic solutions, enabling them to modernize on their terms. Known for its high-touch service, CSI helps financial institutions navigate disruption, strengthen account holder relationships, and drive growth in an increasingly digital-first financial landscape. To learn more, visit www.csiweb.com.

data.title: Crosspoint Capital Partners Adds Former Citi Chief Cloud Officer Clark Smith to Operating Team
data.description:
Veteran technology leader brings rare experience spanning global banking, public service and mission-critical cloud infrastructure to support Crosspoint's portfolio

MENLO PARK, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Crosspoint Capital Partners ("Crosspoint Capital"), an investment firm focused on cybersecurity and its intersection with infrastructure software, today announced the addition of Clark Smith, former Chief Cloud Officer and Head of Cloud Technology Services at Citi , to its operating team.

Smith has spent his career building and operating technology in environments where security, resilience and scale are critical. His experience spans senior technology leadership at major global financial institutions and more than a decade of public service across the Department of Justice, the Intelligence Community and the Department of Homeland Security. That combination gives him a distinctive perspective on what large enterprises require from the technology platforms they depend on.

"Clark is a builder who has operated in environments where technology simply cannot fail. He brings a rare combination of engineering depth, public-sector and intelligence-community experience, and firsthand knowledge of what it takes to run critical infrastructure at global financial scale," said Samir Kapuria, Managing Director of Crosspoint Capital. "That perspective is enormously valuable to our portfolio as we help our companies build platforms that the world's most demanding enterprises can trust."

As an Operating Partner at Crosspoint, Smith will work alongside the firm's investment and portfolio teams, applying his experience in cloud infrastructure, enterprise architecture, security and resilience to technology strategy, platform scaling and the evaluation of emerging technologies. He will also bring the perspective of a large-enterprise technology operator to product strategy and customer value creation.

Prior to joining Crosspoint, Smith served as Chief Cloud Officer and Head of Cloud Technology Services at Citi, where he oversaw global technology infrastructure operations and helped ensure the resilient, secure and cost-effective growth of Citi's enterprise technology architecture. He previously held major technology leadership roles at TD Bank and Deutsche Bank. Before entering financial services, Smith spent more than a decade in public service leading key technology and program initiatives across the Department of Justice, the Intelligence Community and the Department of Homeland Security, where his contributions were recognized with numerous medals and commendations.

"AI and cloud computing are changing what enterprises expect from the software and infrastructure they rely on. Clark has spent his career on the operator side of that equation, responsible for technology in some of the world's most complex environments," said Greg Clark, Managing Partner of Crosspoint Capital. "His combination of technical depth, operational experience and enterprise customer perspective will be incredibly valuable to Crosspoint and our portfolio companies."

Smith joins Crosspoint amid significant growth for the firm. Since its founding in 2020, Crosspoint has grown to $8.6 billion in assets under management and established a differentiated model that combines investment professionals, experienced operating executives and deep sector expertise to provide capabilities and perspective to its portfolio companies.

Crosspoint has invested in companies across network security, endpoint security, digital trust, authentication, software supply chain security, agentic security operations and applied artificial intelligence. Starting in 2025, Crosspoint extended its commitment to cybersecurity innovation by offering each of the Top 10 Finalists in the RSA Conference Innovation Sandbox contest a $5 million uncapped Simple Agreement for Future Equity (SAFE) investment. Recent portfolio outcomes include Cisco's July 2026 acquisition of WideField to boost its Agentic SOC capabilities and F5's September 2025 acquisition of CalypsoAI to bring advanced AI guardrails to large enterprises.

About Crosspoint Capital Partners

Crosspoint Capital is an investment firm focused on the cybersecurity and infrastructure software markets. Crosspoint has assembled a group of successful operators, investors and sector experts to partner with foundational technology companies and drive differentiated returns. Crosspoint has offices in Menlo Park, CA and Boston, MA. For more information, visit www.crosspointcapital.com.

data.title: AlphaCore Wealth Advisory Launches a Separate Family Office Affiliate With the Addition of Streamline Family Office
data.description:
The Streamline team brings more than 25 years of dedicated family office experience and an integrated non-advisory family office model to AlphaCore’s growing platform for ultra-high-net-worth families

LA JOLLA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- AlphaCore Wealth Advisory (“AlphaCore”), a leading independent wealth advisory firm, today announced the launch of AlphaCore Streamline (“AC Streamline”), a dedicated family office affiliate formed through the acquisition of Streamline Family Office (“Streamline”). The move advances the AlphaCore group's national footprint and strategy of building a next-generation wealth management platform while expanding the firm's capabilities for ultra-high-net-worth families through a separate family office affiliate.

Headquartered in Dover, Massachusetts, Streamline is a women-founded and women-led family office, guided for more than 25 years by founder and CEO Katie Sullivan. The firm provides pure, independent family office services to ultra-high-net-worth families and is supported by a 15-person team, including Chief Relationship Officer Amy Johnston; Chief Operating Officer Rebecca Sliwoski, MBA, MS; Chief Financial Officer Trisha Presley, CPA; and Family Advisor Leader Andrea Longo Carter, MBA. The team brings institutional knowledge shaped by years of navigating the complexities of significant wealth and is trusted to coordinate and integrate the financial, operational, and day-to-day needs of families, representing nearly $5 billion in collective assets. Streamline does not select investments, manage portfolios or provide investment advice.

AlphaCore’s addition of AC Streamline builds upon the non-advisory family office foundation the firm has been strengthening over the past several years, including Tara Dekel, Director of AlphaCore Family Office, and reflects the growing demand for services that extend beyond traditional wealth management. AC Streamline marks a strategic move in the AlphaCore group’s evolution, following the expansion of AlphaCore into tax preparation and planning last year.

“I have always believed families deserve something more personal than a menu of services. They need a partner who truly knows their people, priorities, and assets, and who will be there to handle whatever comes up with care, consistency, and discretion. That is the genesis of Streamline, being the one call a family can make and knowing we will take it from there,” said Sullivan. “Our partnership with AlphaCore gives us the opportunity to continue to evolve with our current clients and bring that same level of attention to even more families with greater capabilities.”

As technology and artificial intelligence continue to transform the wealth management industry, machines cannot replicate the trust, discretion, personal relationships, and multi-generational continuity that define the family office experience.

“What makes a true family office relationship different is the level of intimacy and trust it creates. It goes beyond managing investments to understanding the dynamics, priorities, and aspirations of the family,” said Dick Pfister, founder and CEO of AlphaCore. “It is rare to find a team that has spent decades doing this work and has developed the depth of knowledge and relationships that come from that experience. AlphaCore was founded with a vision to provide an enduring boutique, premium client experience, and Streamline is exactly what we were looking for as we continue to build that vision.”

AC Streamline will operate as a separate, affiliated entity providing non-advisory family office services. The existing team will continue to work collaboratively with current and future families' existing wealth advisors, investment managers, and other trusted professional advisors.

“‘Family office’ has become a common phrase in wealth management, but there is an important distinction between offering family office services and operating a dedicated private family office,” said Aidan Walsh, AlphaCore's Head of Corporate Development. “Many firms provide access to specialists and resources. Both AlphaCore and Streamline have spent decades serving families whose needs extend well beyond traditional wealth management through dedicated family office teams and highly personalized service models. What makes this partnership so compelling is the combination of Streamline's twenty-five years of dedicated family office experience with the foundation AlphaCore has already built in this area. Together, we are significantly expanding our capabilities with a team whose experience, trust, and continuity are difficult to replicate.”

The combination expands the AlphaCore group’s ability to serve families across the full continuum of significant wealth, from investment management and planning to tax strategy and the day-to-day coordination of financial lives, while preserving the personal relationships, independence and judgment that have defined Streamline for more than two decades.

Gennari Aronson served as legal counsel to Streamline. Vinson & Elkins served as legal counsel to AlphaCore.

About AlphaCore Wealth Advisory

AlphaCore Wealth Advisory is an independent wealth advisory firm dedicated to helping clients build, preserve, and protect their wealth. Headquartered in La Jolla, California, with offices nationwide, AlphaCore takes a comprehensive approach to wealth planning and strives to deliver sophisticated investment management services by providing access to both traditional and alternative investments. Supported by in-house research, operational resources, and modern technology, AlphaCore advisors place clients’ goals at the center of every financial plan.

data.title: Core Silver Completes Acquisition of Arcus Development Group
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / September 15, 2026 / Core Silver Corp. ( CCOOF ) and Arcus Development Group Inc. ( ARCUF ) ("Arcus", and together with Core Silver ( CCOOF ), the "Companies") are pleased to announce that, further to their prior news releases, Core Silver ( CCOOF ) has completed the previously announced acquisition of all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Arcus (the "Arcus Shares"), effective as of September 15, 2026, by way of a court-approved plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement") under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia).

The Arrangement was completed pursuant to an arrangement agreement between Core Silver ( CCOOF ) and Arcus dated July 9, 2026 (the "Agreement"), and was approved by the Arcus Shareholders at the annual general and special meeting held on August 25, 2026, as well as the Supreme Court of British Columbia on August 28, 2026.

Arrangement Details

Pursuant to the Arrangement, the shareholders of Arcus (the "Arcus Shareholders") are entitled to receive one (1) common share in the authorized capital of Core Silver ( CCOOF ) (each, a "Core Silver Share") in exchange for each one (1) Arcus Share held immediately prior to the closing of the Arrangement (the "Exchange Ratio"). As previously announced, the issued and outstanding convertible securities of Arcus, including share purchase warrants and stock options exercisable for Arcus Shares, were not subject to the Arrangement and, in accordance with their terms and conditions, became exercisable for common shares of Core Silver ( CCOOF ) on their original terms and conditions.

Upon completion of the Arrangement, Core Silver ( CCOOF ) issued 21,221,140 Core Silver Shares to the former Arcus Shareholders as consideration for the Arcus Shares. Accordingly, the former Arcus Shareholders hold approximately 39.2% of the 54,141,705 issued and outstanding Core Silver Shares on a non-diluted basis.

The Core Silver Shares continue to trade on the Canadian Securities Exchange under the symbol "CC". As a result of the Arrangement, Arcus has become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Core Silver ( CCOOF ) and the Arcus Shares are expected to be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange following the close of markets on September 15, 2026. Core Silver ( CCOOF ) intends to cause Arcus to apply to cease to be a reporting issuer in the applicable jurisdictions of Canada.

Full details of the Arrangement, and the exchange of securities thereunder, as described above, are set forth in the management information circular of Arcus dated July 20, 2026 (the "Arcus Circular"), which was mailed to Arcus Shareholders on or about July 31, 2026, and is available on SEDAR+ under Arcus' issuer profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

There is no finder's fee payable by the Companies in connection with the Arrangement.

None of the securities issued pursuant to the Arrangement have been or will be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act"), or any state securities laws, and are being issued in reliance upon available exemptions from such registration requirements pursuant to Section 3(a)(10) of the U.S. Securities Act and applicable exemptions under state securities laws. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any securities.

Leadership and Governance

Pursuant to the Agreement, upon the closing of the Arrangement, Darryl Jones, interim CEO and a director of Arcus, has been appointed as a member of the board of directors of Core Silver ( CCOOF ), and the remaining directors and officers of Arcus have resigned from their respective positions with Arcus. No other changes to the board of directors of Core Silver ( CCOOF ) or its management are currently expected in connection with the Arrangement.

Further Information for Arcus Shareholders

In order to receive Core Silver Shares in exchange for Arcus Shares, registered Arcus Shareholders must complete, sign, date, and return the letter of transmittal that was mailed to each Arcus Shareholder along with the Arcus Circular prior to closing. The letter of transmittal is also available under Arcus' profile on SEDAR+ available at www.sedarplus.ca. Arcus Shareholders whose Arcus Shares are registered in the name of an intermediary, such as a broker, investment dealer, bank, trust company, trust or other intermediary or nominee should contact such nominee for assistance in depositing their Arcus Shares and should follow the instructions of such intermediary or nominee.

Advisors and Legal Counsel

Maarschalk Valuations Inc. acted as financial advisor to Core Silver ( CCOOF ) and its board of directors. Clark Wilson LLP acted as legal counsel to Core Silver ( CCOOF ). Cozen O'Connor LLP acted as legal counsel to Arcus.

Core Silver Corp. ( CCOOF ) is a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on the acquisition and development of mineral projects in British Columbia, Canada. Core Silver ( CCOOF ) currently holds 100% ownership in the Blue Property Mineral Tenure, which covers a land area of 114,074 hectares (~1,140 km²). The project lies within the Atlin Mining District, a well-known gold mining camp located in the unceded territory of the Taku River Tlingit First Nation and the Carcross/Tagish First Nation. The Blue Property hosts a major structural feature known as The Llewellyn Fault Zone ("LFZ"). Core Silver ( CCOOF ) believes that the south Atlin Lake area and the LFZ has been neglected since the last major exploration campaigns in the 1980's. The past 50 years have seen substantial advancements in the understanding of porphyry, skarn, and carbonate replacement type deposits both globally and in British Columbia's Golden Triangle. Core Silver ( CCOOF ) has leveraged this information at the Blue Property Mineral Tenure to tailor an already proven exploration model and believes this could facilitate a major discovery. data.title: Every AI Agent Needs a Kill Switch: DigiCert Launches AI Trust Manager
data.description:
Lehi, Utah, Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- DigiCert, a global leader in intelligent trust, today announced the general availability of DigiCert AI Trust Manager, part of the DigiCert ONE platform. The new solution helps organizations discover and manage the AI agents they own or operate, establish each agent’s verifiable identity and ownership, define what it is authorized to do, and revoke that authority with a kill switch when trust changes.

AI agents can access sensitive data, use software tools, write code, make decisions, and complete transactions with limited human involvement. Yet most enterprise security systems were not built to govern autonomous agents moving across applications, clouds, and organizations at machine speed.

The risks are already emerging. In a July 2026 DigiCert survey of 1,001 IT and cybersecurity leaders, 78% said their organizations had experienced an AI-related security incident or identified an AI vulnerability during the previous year.

“For more than two decades, DigiCert has provided the cryptographic infrastructure that helped the internet scale,” said Amit Sinha, CEO of DigiCert. “We are now bringing that proven trust model to AI agents so organizations can verify who they are, who owns them, and what they are authorized to do.”

Traditional identity systems work like employee badges, establishing trust within a single organization. At the center of DigiCert AI Trust Manager is the DigiCert AI Passport. It’s a portable, cryptographically signed credential that verifies an agent’s identity and connects it to an accountable owner. Policy-based “visas” define which systems, data, and actions the agent may access, as well as how long that authority lasts.

Because the DigiCert AI Passport and its permissions travel with the agent, other systems and organizations can independently verify them without relying on the same identity provider. A receiving organization can deny the agent access within its own environment. If the agent attempts a prohibited action, DigiCert’s automated kill switch blocks it and, under policies set by the agent’s owner or passport issuer, can immediately revoke its authority at the source and quarantine it before harm occurs.

DigiCert AI Trust Manager allows enterprises to:

  • Find and identify agents: Discover AI agents that were purchased, built internally or operating within the business, and connect each one to an accountable owner.
  • Set clear limits: Define the systems, data, and actions an agent may access, and how long its permission remains valid.
  • Extend trust across organizations: Allow other systems and companies to independently verify an agent without requiring both parties to use the same identity provider.
  • Respond when trust changes: Update credentials, expire permissions, or revoke an individual agent or groups of agents upon policy, risks, or any other changes.

"Enterprise AI buying has moved from trust to proof. Buyers are ranking verifiable security controls as their top priority and name unverifiable vendor claims as their top frustration,” said Grace Trinidad, Research Director, AI Security and Trust, IDC. “Cryptographic identity, attestation, and revocation for agents, models, and MCP servers are the machinery that produces this proof, which in turn produces trust, and DigiCert is pointing the identity discipline the internet already runs at scale at exactly that problem."

“As AI agents become more embedded in enterprise workflows, establishing clear identity and accountability will be essential to deploying them responsibly at scale,” said Ajitha Choudary, Vice President of Global Security Engineering & IAM at UKG. “We see DigiCert AI Trust as a promising approach to extending proven principles of digital identity to this new class of autonomous systems. The ability to verify an agent’s identity, define what it is authorized to do, and maintain visibility into its actions could give organizations the foundation they need to adopt agentic AI with greater confidence.”

DigiCert AI Trust Manager is part of DigiCert’s broader AI trust architecture, which applies cryptographic verification across AI agents, models, and content. It complements existing identity and cybersecurity systems by providing a portable foundation for verifying an agent’s identity and authority wherever it operates.

data.title: DevZero Joins AWS ISV Accelerate Program
data.description:
SEATTLE--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- DevZero, a Kubernetes optimization platform that solves for uptime anxiety while addressing ballooning compute and inference costs, announced today that it has joined the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Independent Software Vendor (ISV) Accelerate Program, a co-sell program for AWS Partners that provides software solutions that run on or integrate with AWS. The program helps AWS Partners drive new business by directly connecting participating ISVs with the AWS Sales organization.

Founded in 2022 by two former Uber engineers, DevZero tackles the inefficiencies of Kubernetes environments, specifically the overprovisioning that can lead to out-of-control cloud bills and wasted compute. DevZero optimizes requests at the cluster, node and workload level, maximizing uptime and allowing companies to reclaim 30%+ of their cloud spend in as little as two weeks. Additionally, DevZero’s checkpoint-restore capability allows users to migrate their Kubernetes workloads instantly, in real-time, without restarts.

“Uptime anxiety has driven organizations to spend billions of dollars on extra, idle compute at a time of growing demand and limited capacity. Through the AWS ISV Accelerate Program, we can work with AWS field sellers to help customers improve reliability and performance across their infrastructure without costly overprovisioning,” said Debo Ray, CEO and co-founder of DevZero.

The AWS ISV Accelerate Program provides DevZero with co-sell support and benefits to meet customer needs through collaboration with AWS field sellers globally. Co-selling provides better customer outcomes and assures mutual commitment from AWS and its partners.

Within 10 hours of deploying DevZero, Databahn, an AI-powered data pipeline management platform, achieved approximately 75% cost reduction on an AWS cluster, bringing infrastructure spending in line with revenue targets. Said Mihir Nair, head of architecture, Databahn, “On AWS, DevZero demonstrated they could achieve significantly higher savings than we initially thought possible.”

AWS ISV Accelerate Program members are held to the industry’s highest standards and must undergo a comprehensive evaluation to gain acceptance into the program. DevZero participated in a thorough architectural and security review to ensure the quality and design of our solutions. Proof of customer excellence was also reviewed to validate the successes DevZero customers have achieved across industry verticals.

To learn more about DevZero, visit devzero.io and its customer case studies.

About DevZero

DevZero provides an autonomous compute and inference optimization platform that eliminates the usual tradeoffs between performance, reliability, and cost. The platform profiles, schedules, and rightsizes Kubernetes workloads with zero restarts and picks the best node for every pod, bringing cloud bills back to reality. The result: resilient applications and AI workflows at costs that finally make sense. Based in Seattle, DevZero is backed by Anthos Capital, Foundation Capital, and Madrona. Learn more at devzero.io.

data.title: Sovos Acquires Blue dot, Expanding AI-Native Diagnostics, Workflow, and Intelligence Capabilities, Widening Sovos’ Tax Compliance Platform Technology Lead
data.description:
Acquisition extends Sovos’ Tax Compliance Platform into Travel & Expense and VAT recovery, accelerates agentic diagnosis roadmap with a decade of production AI, and adds an elite data science team with nearly a decade of enterprise ML experience.

ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Sovos, the AI-ready tax compliance company, today announced the acquisition of Blue dot, an AI VAT intelligence and recovery platform headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel. The acquisition strengthens Sovos' strategy in three distinct areas:

  • A proven VAT reclaim business with enterprise distribution through SAP Concur, further strengthening Sovos’ market leading Indirect Tax Suite
  • A production AI platform built on nearly a decade of real-world Machine Learning development in the tax compliance space, bringing differentiated data, models and agentic workflow capabilities to Sovos
  • A world-class data science team that will accelerate Sovos’ AI roadmap from day one, bringing nearly a decade of enterprise ML experience

Blue dot brings advanced AI capabilities that automatically cleanse, validate, enrich and contextualize complex travel & expense (T&E) and accounts payable (AP) transaction data. By turning fragmented spend data into precise, tax-ready intelligence, Blue dot helps enterprises identify eligible VAT and maximize recovery while strengthening compliance.

The Compliance Problem Getting Harder to Ignore

As Continuous Transaction Controls (CTC) expand across Europe, Latin America and Asia, tax compliance is moving from periodic reporting toward real-time transaction validation. CTC frameworks require every B2B invoice to clear a government authority in real time before it can move goods, trigger payment, or support a VAT claim. As a result, businesses need to know not only whether a transaction failed, but why it failed, which upstream business process caused the error and how to prevent it from recurring. This is the diagnosis problem where Blue dot's technology gives Sovos a significant advantage.

Expanding the Tax Compliance Platform into VAT Recovery

Blue dot's core business is enterprise VAT recovery across Travel & Expense (T&E) and Accounts Payable (AP). Its platform uses AI to extract, cleanse, validate, enrich and contextualize transaction data across invoices, receipts, and expense reports. Agents turn fragmented spend data into clean, tax-ready intelligence that helps enterprises identify eligible VAT and maximize legitimate recovery while strengthening compliance.

Blue dot serves hundreds of enterprise customers globally across banking and finance, consumer goods, retail and manufacturing, and has achieved SAP Concur Endorsed App status. The platform has demonstrated greater than 98% accuracy across VAT and taxable employee benefits lifecycles, with a five-year average customer tenure and approximately 99% recurring revenue.

Accelerating AI Across the Sovos Platform

Sovos has spent two decades building trusted tax compliance infrastructure, connecting businesses to governments and embedding compliant tax workflows into the enterprise systems where transactions originate. With the launch of Sovos Intelligence earlier this summer, Sovos introduced an intelligence layer that brings AI-powered insight to the transaction level.

Blue dot extends that capability upstream, using AI to transform fragmented transaction data into clean, contextualized data for better tax decisions. Its platform includes more than 150 purpose-built AI models, a real-time orchestration engine, a transaction Knowledge Graph and agentic capabilities designed to automate document ingestion, reconciliation and compliance operations.

Sovos intends to embed Blue dot's AI into its compliance transaction flow, accelerating its diagnosis capabilities toward a system that not only identifies which rule failed, but explains why the underlying business event was wrong and what needs to change upstream to prevent it from recurring.

The acquisition also strengthens Sovos’ ability to prepare customers for ViDA and evolving CTC mandates. Blue dot’s AI will reconcile structured B2B invoices that increasingly move through regulated channels with employee expenses and corporate card transactions that originate at the point of sale. This will help Sovos customers prevent duplicate or inconsistent VAT reporting while connecting the full transaction picture to the compliance network.

“Blue dot has built something genuinely rare — an AI engine purpose-built to understand the complexity and context hidden inside enterprise transaction data,” said Kevin Akeroyd, CEO, Sovos. “Its combination of tax intelligence and agentic technology gives us a powerful foundation to accelerate our broader AI strategy. Just as importantly, we are adding a talented team that has spent nearly a decade building AI in production at enterprise scale.”

World-Class AI Talent

Blue dot’s data science and engineering teams will join Sovos’ product and technology organization, bringing nearly a decade of production AI and machine learning experience built on real enterprise transaction data, at real scale and across real jurisdictions. The team of engineers and data scientists brings deep expertise in building, training and deploying AI and machine learning for complex tax and transaction data.

About Sovos

The Sovos Tax Compliance Cloud enables businesses to identify, determine, and report on every tax obligation globally. Sovos processes more than 70 billion transactions per year across 150+ countries, serving more than 100,000 customers - including half the Fortune 500. Learn more at sovos.com.

data.title: The Oasis Group Publishes New White Paper on Meeting Management as a Profitability Driver in Wealth Management
data.description:
FORT MILL, S.C., Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Oasis Group, the leading research and consulting firm specializing in the wealth management and financial technology sectors, today announced the release of its new white paper, Why Meeting Management Is a Profitability Problem in Wealth Management, sponsored by GReminders. The paper examines how the administrative work surrounding client meetings — scheduling, preparation, note capture, and follow-up — has become a direct and measurable drag on advisor capacity and firm profitability, and offers a practical framework advisory firms can use to diagnose and close the gap.

The research challenges the industry's default framing of scalability as an advisor problem to be solved by extending advisor reach. Instead, the paper argues that firms are resource-centric, and that the true constraint on growth is whether the team around the advisor runs a designed process or simply reacts to whatever the advisor generates. Meeting management, treated as an end-to-end lifecycle rather than a collection of individual tasks, is identified as the surface where this dynamic plays out most visibly and most expensively.

“The firms that will scale over the next decade are not the ones with the most talented advisors,” said John O’Connell, Chief Executive Officer of The Oasis Group. “They are the ones whose meeting management and client engagement process would survive the departure of any single person in the building, including the founders or a key partner advisor.”

Key Findings

The white paper anchors its argument in three data points:

  • Advisors lose more than a full business day a week to administrative work. Cerulli Associates reports that advisors spend 9 of 40 work-week hours on administrative tasks, with ineffective delegation to staff cited as a major productivity challenge for 60 percent of advisors.
  • M&A buyers are pricing firms on process, not personality. Wealth management M&A activity hit a record 466 announced transactions in 2025, up 27.3 percent from 2024, with acquirers increasingly evaluating whether a practice runs consistently without any one person holding it together.
  • Key-person dependency carries a steep, hidden price tag. Replacing a single team member who has been informally holding a process together can cost 50 to 200 percent of that person's annual salary once recruiting, training, and lost institutional knowledge are factored in.

A Three-Part Framework

Rather than prescribing a single tool or vendor, the paper offers advisory firms a diagnostic framework built around three steps:

  • Measure what the process actually costs using a two-week time log across booking, rescheduling, capture, and follow-up to establish a factual baseline rather than a general impression.
  • Ask the right questions before evaluating AI tools, including whether a solution writes to the firm's system of record, where a human reviews output before it becomes client-facing, and whether the firm's data and workflows remain portable if the vendor relationship ends.
  • Sequence technology onto the process, not around it, fixing workflow ownership and escalation paths first so automation compounds a firm's strengths rather than its gaps.

The paper also addresses the compliance question directly, noting that firms carry record-keeping and supervisory obligations under FINRA Rule 3110 and SEC Rule 206(4)-7 regardless of whether meeting notes are handwritten or AI-generated, and that informal, undocumented processes — not systemized ones with proper consent and review — represent the greater unpriced risk.

“Meetings are the heartbeat of the advisor-client engagement experience,” O’Connell said. “Firms that treat meeting management as a designed, end-to-end process are positioned to grow without adding more expensive people to compensate for gaps a system could close instead.”

The white paper offers tailored implications for independent RIAs and solo practices, multi-advisor practices, and aggregators or enterprises, recognizing that the stakes and starting points for closing the meeting management gap differ by firm type and scale.

About The Oasis Group

The Oasis Group is a leading research and consulting firm specializing in the wealth management and financial technology sectors. The firm provides in-depth market analysis, strategic guidance, and implementation expertise to help organizations evaluate technology solutions and drive business growth.

For more information or to access the full white paper, visit https://theoasisgrp.com/

data.title: Nexcess Expands Managed Cloud Services with New Disaster Recovery Offering

Nexcess now delivers managed disaster recovery with a continuously running, verified off-site copy of your server, powered by Acronis cyber protection technology.

LANSING, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nexcess, a managed cloud provider, today announced the expansion of its current Acronis backed suite of products with managed disaster recovery. This extends the company's existing Acronis-powered backup service by giving businesses a live, bootable copy of their server standing by in the cloud. This includes 1 hour Recovery Time Objectives (RTO), automated provisioning on a pre-configured network, and proven readiness by automated test failovers.

Most businesses skip disaster recovery because the traditional version requires a second site, a replication stack, and someone to own it. This is one agent. Nexcess provisions resources available in the environment, verifies the connectivity, and runs the test failovers. For customers already backing up with Nexcess, the agent is already there.

"A backup protects your data. Disaster recovery protects your business," said Michael Ohayon, General Manager, Managed Cloud, Nexcess. "Most businesses find out the difference the hard way, in the middle of a ransomware attack or a hardware failure, when they realize a restore is going to take hours they don't have. We built this so a customer's server is never more than click of a button away from being back online, and so they can see proof it works before they ever need it."

Why now

Ransomware, hardware failure, and compliance reviews are pushing more small and midsize businesses to confront a gap they didn't know they had: their nightly backups protect their files, but not their uptime. When disaster strikes, rebuilding a server from a snapshot takes time, stretching resources and putting revenue at risk. A disaster recovery service closes that gap by keeping a running copy ready to take over in minutes rather than hours.

Availability

Disaster recovery is available starting September 14, 2026. Nexcess customers already running backups can access disaster recovery as an add-on, and new customers can bundle it with our managed cloud solutions.

MIAMI, FL, Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NextNRG, Inc. Developed to manage EzFill’s own mobile fueling operations, the platform is currently deployed across the Company’s fleet of 141 trucks operating in 15 markets. The technology brings together routing, scheduling, driver and route performance, real-time truck fuel levels and fuel delivery data in a single operating system, giving managers detailed visibility into fleet activity and fuel movement.

"We built this technology to solve problems we face every day in our own operation," said Yehuda Levy, CEO of EzFill. "It gives our managers visibility into how our trucks are being routed, how drivers are performing, how much fuel is on each truck and how much fuel is being delivered at every stop. We believe other fleet and fuel operators face many of the same challenges, and we are now preparing to license the platform, including a white-label version that can be adapted for their operations."

"The strongest validation we've received comes from our largest customer, one of the world's largest online retailers, which views our platform and its integration with their back-end systems as a differentiator, and has encouraged us to make it available to its other fueling providers. When a customer of that scale tells you your software is the reason they work with you, it says something about the technology," said Michael D. Farkas, Founder and CEO of NextNRG ( NXXT ). "EzFill developed this platform to optimize its own operations, and it has become integral to how we manage the fleet. We believe the same technology can help other fleet and fuel operators improve visibility, efficiency and accountability across their operations."

Unlike conventional fleet tracking systems that primarily monitor vehicle location, EzFill’s platform connects routing, operational and fuel data to provide a more complete view of each route and delivery. The system evaluates planned routes against those actually driven, identifies deviations and additional stops, and uses live fuel volumes on each truck to help managers plan routes based on available fuel, scheduled stops and delivery requirements.

At the fuel-delivery level, the platform adds another layer of accountability by tracking fuel throughout the delivery process. It monitors fuel levels within EzFill’s trucks, fuel delivered at each stop and vehicle-level fuel data captured through EzFill’s Bluetooth-enabled fuel monitoring technology, allowing the system to reconcile fuel moving into and out of each truck and compare delivered volumes against the receiving vehicle’s fuel level.

Licensing the platform represents an opportunity for EzFill to extend technology developed for its own operations to a broader market. Initial interest from fleet and fuel operators has been strong, and the Company is in active discussions with prospective licensees. data.title: CenterPoint Energy discloses customer data breach in SEC filing
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - CenterPoint Energy ( CNP ) said in an SEC filing on Monday that the company had become aware in September of an online post by a third party claiming to have obtained a dataset of information on some of its customers.

* The Texas-based utility said it activated its cybersecurity incident response protocols and enlisted third-party cybersecurity experts after learning of the post, while also taking steps to further protect its systems.

* The company said its investigation determined that an unauthorized third party obtained personal information relating to a portion of its customers through one of its external-facing systems.

* CenterPoint said its electric and gas services have not been affected and remain operational, and it does not currently believe the incident is reasonably likely to have a material impact on its financial condition or the results of its operations.

* It has incurred and expects to continue incurring expenses tied to the incident and its response, the utility said, adding that it carries cybersecurity insurance it believes will offset related costs.

* "Our filing speaks for itself," a CenterPoint Energy ( CNP ) spokesperson said on Tuesday when Reuters reached out to the company with a request for comment.

(Reporting by Dharna Bafna and Pooja Menon in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid and Pooja Desai)

NEW HOPE, Pa., Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Orchestra BioMed Holdings, Inc. This second payment follows the approximately $5 million upfront payment received in January 2026 and brings total cash proceeds received by Orchestra BioMed ( OBIO ) from the transaction to approximately $11 million.

Vivasure, an Ireland-based company pioneering next-generation technology for percutaneous vessel closure, had been a strategic holding of Orchestra BioMed ( OBIO ) since the Company’s formation. Haemonetics ( HAE ) completed its acquisition of Vivasure on January 9, 2026, as previously announced.

The payment completes the approximately $11 million in proceeds previously disclosed as expected during 2026. Orchestra BioMed ( OBIO ) remains eligible to receive up to approximately $10 million in additional proceeds through future revenue earnouts, subject to the achievement of certain milestones, for total potential proceeds of up to $21 million.

Developed by Vivasure, the PerQseal® Elite system uses a proprietary bioabsorbable patch to seal large-bore arteriotomies and venotomies from inside the vessel, offering a sutureless, fully absorbable solution for structural heart and endovascular procedures. PerQseal Elite is not available for sale in the United States.

About Orchestra BioMed ( OBIO )

Orchestra BioMed ( OBIO ) is a biomedical innovation company accelerating high-impact technologies to patients through strategic collaborations with market-leading global medical device companies. The Company’s two flagship product candidates - Atrioventricular Interval Modulation (AVIM) Therapy and Virtue® Sirolimus AngioInfusion™ Balloon (Virtue SAB) - are currently undergoing pivotal clinical trials for their lead indications, each representing multi-billion-dollar annual global market opportunities. AVIM Therapy is a bioelectronic treatment for hypertension, the leading risk factor for death worldwide, and is designed to be delivered by a pacemaker and achieve immediate, substantial and sustained reductions in blood pressure in patients with hypertensive heart disease. The Company has a strategic collaboration with Medtronic, one of the largest medical device companies in the world and the global leader in cardiac pacing therapies, for the development and commercialization of AVIM Therapy for the treatment of uncontrolled hypertension in pacemaker-indicated patients. AVIM Therapy has FDA Breakthrough Device Designations for these patients, as well as an estimated 7.7 million total patients in the U.S. with uncontrolled hypertension despite medical therapy and increased cardiovascular risk. data.title: ZONDISION Introduces Glasses-Free 3D Developer Ecosystem at PAX West 2026
data.description:
The ZIMO M1 display, ZimoMatrix content conversion engine, ZimoInstant content conversion engine, and ZimoClaw platform integrate glasses-free 3D display technology, content conversion capabilities, and developer tooling into a cohesive ecosystem.

SEATTLE and NEW YORK and SILICON VALLEY, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ZONDISION, a comprehensive innovator in glasses-free light-field display technology, debuted its flagship light-field monitor, the ZIMO M1, at PAX West 2026. Concurrently, the company launched three developer-centric offerings: the ZimoMatrix game conversion engine, the ZimoInstant image and video conversion engine, and ZimoClaw, a platform for light-field gaming experiences.

Complementing the product unveilings, ZONDISION officially inaugurated its Global Developer Program, granting access to low-level optical interfaces, its proprietary rendering SDK, and fundamental spatial imaging functionalities. This initiative aims to empower developers and content creation teams globally to generate and deploy high-fidelity light-field 3D content with enhanced efficiency.

At PAX West, the ZIMO M1 served as the display technology for a public demonstration area featuring over 100 games enhanced for light-field 3D, drawing consistent engagement from players and developers throughout the exhibition. Furthermore, ZONDISION engaged in numerous preliminary partnership discussions with international game development studios during the event.

Leveraging ZONDISION's proprietary ASIC technology, low-latency eye-tracking systems, and switchable 2D/3D display capabilities, the ZIMO M1 facilitates seamless transitions between conventional 2D and glasses-free 3D viewing modes. It preserves native image fidelity in 2D mode and minimizes crosstalk in 3D, obviating the need for eyewear to deliver a more natural and accessible stereoscopic gaming and media experience. Attendees at PAX frequently remarked on the heightened sense of depth and dimensionality perceived when viewing familiar games rendered in light-field 3D.

Collectively, ZimoMatrix, ZimoInstant, and ZimoClaw constitute an end-to-end toolchain for the creation, optimization, and consumption of content on ZONDISION's light-field display platforms.

**ZimoMatrix: Facilitating the Transition of Existing Games to Light-Field 3D**

ZimoMatrix functions as ZONDISION's engine for 3D game development and conversion. Its design prioritizes enabling developers and ZONDISION engineers to integrate existing game titles into the glasses-free 3D ecosystem rather than serving as a foundational game development engine.

Compatible with leading game development environments such as Unreal Engine and Unity, ZimoMatrix provides functionalities for 3D rendering, conversion, depth and view processing, compatibility optimization, and the generation of Game 3D Profiles.

**ZimoInstant: Enhancing Accessibility in 3D Content Creation**

ZimoInstant is an image and video conversion utility engineered to broaden the accessibility of light-field content production. It enables the conversion of standard images, recorded video footage, and other visual media into 3D output compatible with light-field displays.

By streamlining the conversion process, ZimoInstant empowers developers and content creators to produce 3D visual assets without necessitating intricate professional production workflows.

**ZimoClaw: Orchestrating the Comprehensive 3D Gaming Experience**

ZimoClaw represents ZONDISION's player-oriented platform for managing and optimizing the complete light-field gaming experience.

This platform offers full-lifecycle management services, including Game 3D Profile administration, tunable visual parameter settings, game management, compatibility optimization, troubleshooting protocols, and profile updates, thereby ensuring a stable and optimized light-field 3D experience for each supported game.

ZimoClaw also provides users access to an expanding catalog of games and 3D content specifically optimized for ZONDISION displays.

**A New Global Developer Program**

In conjunction with its new software tools, ZONDISION announced the Global Developer Program, through which the company intends to extend access to its foundational spatial technologies to a worldwide developer community.

The program encompasses access to ZONDISION's rendering SDK, optical interfaces, and spatial imaging capabilities, with support for development environments and standards including Unity, Unreal Engine, C++, and OpenXR.

By making these capabilities available, ZONDISION also aims to advance glasses-free 3D technology beyond the gaming sector into domains such as digital creation, AI-generated content, professional visualization, and other interactive applications.

**Transitioning from Superior Displays to a Sustainable 3D Ecosystem**

ZONDISION's core technical team comprises optical engineers and algorithm specialists with over a decade of expertise in stereoscopic display technologies. The company's end-to-end research and development capabilities encompass optical architecture, custom light-field display ASICs, eye tracking, 3D rendering, and spatial imaging algorithms.

Earlier this year, the ZIMO M1 successfully concluded a Kickstarter campaign, earning a "Project We Love" designation and exceeding its initial funding target by over 2,368%, with contributions from backers across more than 20 countries and regions.

The historical challenge for 3D has not solely been the development of superior display hardware; a sustainable ecosystem necessitates accessible development tools, a robust content library, and intuitive user pathways for content discovery and interaction.

ZONDISION is addressing these interconnected challenges holistically: ZIMO provides the display platform; ZimoMatrix and ZimoInstant facilitate content creation and conversion; ZimoClaw bridges content with users; and the Global Developer Program democratizes access to the underlying technology for a broader creator base.

For 3D to achieve mainstream integration in daily computing, it requires more than enhanced displays; it demands a comprehensive ecosystem. ZONDISION is actively constructing such an ecosystem.

**About ZONDISION**

ZONDISION is a full-stack company specializing in glasses-free light-field display technology. Its capabilities span optical design, custom 3D processing, eye tracking, spatial rendering, display hardware, developer SDKs, conversion utilities, and content solutions. The company's technologies and products support a wide array of applications, including gaming, media, CAD, medical visualization, education, AIGC, and other professional and consumer use cases.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were 0.3% lower, S&P 500 futures were down 0.2%, and Nasdaq futures were 0.1% lower.

data.title: Study Finds Healthcare Concern Jumps From 31% to 74% After Federal Debt Connection Is Explained
data.description:
Black Book's national consumer study finds nearly one-third would borrow, delay care or skip treatment if annual household healthcare costs increased by $1,000; full report available complimentary to industry stakeholders and media.

WASHINGTON, D.C. / ACCESS Newswire / September 15, 2026 / Black Book Research today announced the publication of "The $40 Trillion Healthcare Question: National Healthcare Consumer Awareness, Expectations & Household Resilience Study," examining how Americans understand and believe they would experience the healthcare consequences of sustained federal fiscal pressure. The Q3 2026 study reports online and panel findings from 1,500 U.S. adults age 18 and older in Q3.

The study identifies a substantial Healthcare Fiscal Awareness Gap: just 31% initially expressed concern about the potential personal healthcare implications of the federal government's financial condition. After respondents received a brief explanation of federal debt, interest costs and competing healthcare commitments, 74% expressed concern, a 43-percentage-point increase.

"Washington debates trillions. Families make decisions about prescriptions, premiums and whether they can afford the next appointment," said Doug Brown, Founder of Black Book Research. "This study brings those conversations together. The question for policymakers is not simply how to improve the federal balance sheet. It is how to do so without making necessary healthcare less affordable or harder to obtain."

Initial awareness and concern were measured before respondents received explanatory information. That statement specifically told respondents that fiscal pressure does not make any particular healthcare cut or tax increase automatic. The findings describe consumer perceptions, expectations and anticipated household responses, not evidence that federal debt has caused a specific medical bill or coverage reduction.

Another $1,000 Could Change Whether Households Seek Care

The study's household stress test translates a national fiscal debate into a concrete affordability question: what would respondents do if their household's annual healthcare costs increased by $1,000?

Thirty-two percent said they would borrow money, delay medical care or skip medications or treatment. Another 25% would reduce other household spending, and 18% would draw on savings. Only 7% said they could absorb the increase without significant change. The hypothetical cost increase was not attributed exclusively to federal debt.

"A federal savings estimate is not a complete healthcare policy," Brown said. "Every proposal should explain who pays more, whose coverage changes and whether patients can still get care. Moving an expense off Washington's books does not make it disappear from a family's budget. When consumers say another $1,000 would push them toward borrowing or foregoing treatment, policymakers should treat that as a warning, not a rounding error."

Consumers Anticipate Higher Costs and Greater Pressure on Access

Looking ahead five to ten years, 68% of respondents expect sustained federal fiscal pressure to contribute to higher household insurance or out-of-pocket healthcare costs, while 62% anticipate higher Medicare premiums or cost sharing.

Concern also extends beyond affordability. Fifty-five percent expect fewer clinicians to accept Medicare or Medicaid; 49% anticipate greater financial pressure on rural hospitals or vulnerable service lines; and 46% expect reduced subsidies or benefits. These are respondents' expectations about potential consequences, not forecasts that those outcomes will occur.

Among respondents age 50 and older, 61% were not very confident or not at all confident that Medicare would provide benefits at approximately today's level when they need them. Among Medicaid enrollees, 57% worried that future budget pressure could reduce access to participating clinicians or services.

"An insurance card is not the same thing as access to care," Brown said. "The consumer test is whether there is an affordable appointment, an available clinician and a service within reach. Protecting Medicare and Medicaid should mean examining that entire experience-not merely preserving a program's name while leaving patients to navigate higher costs or fewer options."

A Generational Warning, but No Consensus on Who Should Pay

The findings also reveal concern about the durability of the federal healthcare promise. Among adults ages 18 to 34, 72% expect Medicare benefits to be less generous when their generation needs them. Across the overall sample, 70% agreed that today's federal borrowing unfairly transfers future healthcare and tax obligations to younger generations.

However, agreement about the burden does not translate into agreement about the solution. Asked whether they would personally accept somewhat higher federal taxes today if doing so materially reduced the likelihood of future Medicare or Medicaid cuts, 44% said yes, 41% said no and 15% were unsure.

A separate question requiring respondents to choose their preferred fiscal response produced another divided result. The largest group, 34%, preferred reducing other federal spending before healthcare. Twenty-two percent favored higher taxes to preserve Medicare and Medicaid benefits; 16% preferred reducing payments to health plans and providers; and 10% would continue borrowing rather than reduce healthcare spending.

Options involving direct consumer losses attracted smaller shares: 7% preferred higher beneficiary premiums or cost sharing, 4% a higher Medicare eligibility age, and 3% reduced benefits or Medicaid eligibility. No single option commanded majority support.

"No party should mistake concern about federal debt for public consent to its preferred healthcare solution," Brown said. "These findings are not a blank check for higher taxes, benefit cuts or continued borrowing. Leaders of both parties owe the public an explanation of the tradeoffs: what changes, who bears the cost, how access is protected and what younger Americans can reasonably expect in return for the taxes they pay."

Complimentary Report Available to Industry Stakeholders and Media: The full 32-page report includes national findings, healthcare affordability and access expectations, generational comparisons, policy preferences, consumer indices, the survey instrument and methodology.

"The $40 Trillion Healthcare Question: National Healthcare Consumer Awareness, Expectations & Household Resilience Study" is available for complimentary download to industry stakeholders and members of the media at:

blackbookmarketresearch.com/the-black-book-national-consumer-study

The study reports findings from 1,500 U.S. adults age 18 and older during Q3 2026. Its methodology describes a national online-panel design, demographic quota controls and post-stratification to U.S. adult population benchmarks. Initial awareness and concern were measured before respondents received the fiscal-healthcare explanation. Results reflect self-reported perceptions, expectations and intended behavior rather than demonstrated economic outcomes or causal effects.

About Black Book Research

Black Book Research is an independent market research organization focused on global healthcare technology, services, operations and stakeholder experience. Since 2003, Black Book has conducted research across healthcare delivery, revenue cycle management, payer technology, clinical systems, managed services and emerging digital-health categories in U.S. and international markets. Its consumer and stakeholder research examines developments affecting healthcare buyers, users, policymakers, investors and the public through a vendor-agnostic research model.

data.title: Stocks wobble but no sign of panic as yields surge
data.description:
Sept 15 (Reuters) - Add the summer bond-market rout to the list of market upheavals that U.S. stocks have largely shrugged off.

Despite a sharp rise in U.S. Treasury and overseas government bond yields over the past few weeks, the S&P 500 sits just less than 3% below its August 13 record high, as the promise of AI-driven profit growth and economic resilience prompts investors to buy the dips - and perhaps limits the impulse to rotate into bonds.

Investors are watching if the calm lasts. The last time the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5% was October 2023. That one-day episode was accompanied by a mild selloff in stocks. A more sustained rise above 5% in 2007, in the run-up to the global financial crisis, came just before the S&P 500 shed nearly 5% over two months and much more later.

Here's a look at what's helping stocks:

AI TRADE GOING STRONG

Rising yields typically pressure high-growth stocks because much of their appeal lies in expectations for future profits whose value diminishes as discount rates climb.

This time around, some tech behemoths such as Apple and Microsoft ( MSFT ) are trading just below their record highs as the AI boom shows few signs of slowing and earnings keep surging.

High-flying chip stocks have lost some shine in recent months, including a broad pullback on Monday, driven in part by concerns about a possible slowdown in domestic AI investment, but some say for now it is a natural move after eye-popping gains earlier in the year.

"We're leaning more into semiconductors; we think there's going to be an even tighter supply-demand dynamic next year when it comes to memory," said Laura Cooper, global investment strategist and head of macro credit at Nuveen.

SOLID EARNINGS GROWTH

Second-quarter earnings for S&P 500 companies are expected to have grown 53% year-on-year, or 49.5% excluding the energy sector, according to LSEG I/B/E/S data. Profits are expected to jump 35% in 2026, up sharply from the 14% growth last year.

Both Alphabet and Amazon reported strong growth in their cloud computing businesses on the back of the AI boom. Stripping out mark-to-market gains at the two companies, the adjusted growth rate is 35%.

"The double headwinds of rising bond yields and oil prices are now testing the market's resilience, but stocks have not lost their key pillar of support, which is fast-rising earnings," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist-investment strategy at Edward Jones.

ECONOMY HUMMING ALONG

The U.S. economy has stood resilient despite the price pressures stemming from the Iran war.

U.S. job growth accelerated sharply in August, suggesting an improvement in the labor market as employment in leisure and hospitality rebounded after two straight monthly declines.

"Consumers, labor markets and corporate balance sheets have generally held up better than feared. Many investors spent the past three years expecting recession. Instead, they got slower but positive growth," said analysts at Aberdeen.

Inflation pressures have been running high, but consumer spending remains robust, though customers are seeking lower-cost alternatives.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis last month revised up consumer spending estimates to 3.4% from the originally reported 3.2%, in an indication that the individual consumption that supports two-thirds of U.S. economic activity had held up through the first half of the year.

SMALL CAPS A BRIGHT SPOT

Smaller firms often rely on external borrowing to fund their operations, making them vulnerable to higher interest rates.

Despite that sensitivity, the Russell 2000 index of smaller U.S. companies has sharply outperformed the benchmark S&P 500 this year, helped by strong earnings and as investors sought exposure to parts of the market beyond high-growth technology stocks.

While the higher yields have weighed on the small-cap stocks recently, driving the index down more than 5% from its mid-August record high, many expect the momentum to continue.

"Almost all of the lead was built in the first half, when the domestic growth story was doing the heavy lifting: reshoring, an M&A pickup, deregulation and earnings that are far more levered to the U.S. economy than to the mega-cap AI trade," said Tracy Shuchart, senior economist at NinjaTrader.

"If the Fed holds, that is a tailwind for the Russell, because the group has the most to gain the moment the market stops pricing higher for longer."

STOCKS-BONDS CORRELATION TURNS POSITIVE

Typically, in unfavorable economic situations, investors chase the safety of bonds while risk assets, such as stocks, tend to fall.

This time, the Iran conflict has driven up oil prices and fueled interest-rate hike expectations, triggering a bond-market rout that pushed government bond yields to multi-year highs globally as investors demanded more premium to hold debt.

Analysts note that a positive correlation between stocks and bonds emerged post the COVID-19 pandemic-induced inflation shock. This implies stocks and bonds could move in the same direction, dimming the appeal of bonds as a safer investment compared to stocks.

"Given that sovereign bonds no longer diversify or hedge risk assets as effectively, allocations to bonds have been falling while investors have turned to short-term hedging strategies," strategists at HSBC said in a note.

"Allocations to equities have soared, supporting higher valuations."

(Reporting by Purvi Agarwal, Medha Singh, Sruthi Shankar, Utkarsh Tushar Hathi, Sudeshna Ghoshal in Bengaluru, editing by Colin Barr and Sriraj Kalluvila)

Increasing vehicle complexity, technician shortages, rising costs and rapidly evolving customer expectations are putting pressure on traditional operating models. What distinguishes ShopCentral is not simply the number of workflows it brings together, but the intelligence, scalability, connectivity and AI-driven innovation behind them. Designed for enterprise organizations and independent repairers alike, the platform connects repair order management, digital inspections, customer communications, payments, reporting and business operations while integrating with capabilities such as Solera’s multi award-winning Identifix Direct-Hit®. Instead of forcing repairers to move between disconnected systems, manually transfer information or piece together data to understand what is happening in the business, ShopCentral creates a connected operating environment where information moves seamlessly across workflows, teams and locations. This gives technicians faster access to the information they need, gives managers greater visibility into performance, and enables businesses to identify opportunities, address issues, and make better decisions faster. Just as importantly, that connected data creates the foundation for AI to deliver increasingly powerful intelligence and automation throughout the repair process — helping shops improve productivity, strengthen customer engagement and operate more profitably.

For enterprise operators, the challenge is becoming increasingly complex. Growing vehicle complexity, technician shortages, rising labor and operating costs, margin pressure and increasing customer expectations are colliding with an operating model that, for many organizations, still relies on fragmented technology, inconsistent processes and limited visibility across locations. Managing dozens or hundreds of shops through separate systems makes it harder to standardize operations, understand performance, deploy technology consistently and identify where revenue or productivity is being lost. ShopCentral changes that equation. A single cloud-based platform gives enterprise operators centralized visibility and control across the organization while enabling consistent workflows, reporting and performance management at every location. Leaders can see what is happening across the business, benchmark performance, identify opportunities and scale best practices without stitching together information from multiple systems. And because ShopCentral is built as an intelligent, connected platform, new capabilities and AI-driven innovation can be deployed across the enterprise without adding another layer of technology or complexity.

For individual shops, the value is equally clear: one place for the tools, information and intelligence needed to run the business, without the complexity and cost of managing multiple systems. data.title: FOREX-Dollar ticks up as oil prices climb, Fed rate hike chances firm
data.description:
(Updates prices throughout)

* Treasury 10-year yield climbs to highest since 2007

* Fed hike on Wednesday seen as done deal

* Dollar strength pushes kiwi to two-month low

* Yen falls to 155 for first time in a week

By Shashwat Chauhan and Jiaxing Li

Sept 15 (Reuters) - The euro was pinned at one-month lows against a broadly strengthening dollar on Tuesday, as surging oil prices lifted Treasury yields and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates this week.

Benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yields surged to their highest since 2007, last up 4.1 basis points on the day to 5.004%.

Oil prices held near a four-month peak, standing at over $105 a barrel, after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia and Gulf-Iran talks were postponed.

Markets now see a Fed hike on Wednesday as a near certainty, with CME's FedWatch tool pricing in a more than 92% chance of an interest-rate increase.

"It's quite likely they will hike at this point. What's happening in the bond market is a warning signal, and if they decide to hold rates at this stage, it can lead to unwanted turmoil," said Francesco Pesole, FX strategist at ING.

"From an FX perspective, we see it as a positive event for the dollar."

Pressured by broad dollar strength, the euro slipped 0.1% to $1.154, hovering near its lowest since August 14.

Sterling weakened 0.1% to $1.348 ahead of a Bank of England interest rate decision on Thursday where consensus is widely tilted towards a hold, though future rate hikes are expected by year-end, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Data on Tuesday showed Britain's jobs market stayed weak, with vacancies at a four-year low and pay growth steady.

The yen also pulled away from a seven-month high, leaving the dollar up roughly 0.3% at 154.8 ahead of an expected Bank of Japan rate hike on Friday. It briefly weakened past 155 for the first time in a week earlier on.

Market sentiment on the yen is starting to shift, with speculators turning to a net long position on the Japanese currency for the first time since February.

The New Zealand dollar dipped 0.2%, hitting a two-month low, while the Australian dollar was 0.1% lower at $0.713.

The dollar's six-currency index rose 0.1% to 99.58, standing near its highest in about two weeks, also gaining support from weakened risk appetite as stock markets fell.

RATE HIKES AWAITED

The renewed energy-induced inflation pressures follow a U.S. jobs report that was much stronger than expected and a pickup in consumer prices for August, strengthening market conviction that the Fed will raise rates on Wednesday.

Economists polled by Reuters also expect at least one more hike by the end of March, reversing a fragile no-change consensus prior to Friday's official data showing firm inflation.

"If the Fed is viewed as beginning a new hiking cycle rather than calibrating monetary policy, monetary policy could have spillovers to risk assets," Gabriele Foà, a portfolio manager at Algebris Investments said in a note.

The offshore yuan was flat at 6.712 per dollar, hovering near its strongest in more than three years, after data showing China's industrial sector regained strength in August, though consumption remained sluggish.

(Reporting by Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Shashwat Chauhan in Bengaluru; Editing by Amanda Cooper, Jan Harvey and Chizu Nomiyama )

data.title: Former Mossad Chief, Yossi Cohen, Strategic Advisor to SoftBank, Joins Quantum X Labs as President of Scientific Advisory Board
